page.layout: One printed page (page 7). Running head at top centre. Below it a heading line, then verse in the main column with a heading in the middle, then verse below. Marginal notes in the right margin, beside the verse. Signature mark "A 4" at the foot right, under the text.

p.i: Martius huic sonipes campos hinnitibus implet,
Hinc iuga cornipedes erecti bellica raptant:
Non Elaeus erat campo feruentior axis.
Prodiga gens animæ,
properare facillima mortem.
Nanque vbi transcendit florentes viribus annos,
Impatiens aui spernit nouisse senectam.
Et fati modus in dextra est: hic omne metallum:
p.note: Hispani gēs Martia. Metallis abū dat Hispa-nia. Chalybem profert. Asturia. Aurifera est.
p.i: Electri gemino pallent de semine venæ,
Atque atros chalybis fœtus humus horrida nutrit.
Sed scelerum causas operit Deus. Astur auarus
Visceribus lacera telluris mergitur imis,
Et redit infœlix effosso concolor auro.
Hinc certant Pattole tibi Duriasque, Tagusque,
p.note: Durias fl. Tagus fl. Grauij popu-li. Lethe fl. Fertilis His-pania.
p.i: Quisque super Grauios lucentes voluit arenas
Infernas populis referens obliuia Lethes.
Nec Cereri terra indocilis, nec inhospita Baccho,
Nullaque Palladia sese magis arbore tollit.
Necnon totus adest vesper, populique reposti.
p.note: sil. Ital. lib. 3. Cantabri & eorum mo-res.
p.i: Cantaber ante omnes hyemisque, æstúsque, famisque
Inuictus, palmámque, ex omni ferre labore.
Mirus amor populo (cum pigra incanuit ætas)
Imbelles iam dudum annos prauertere saxo:
Nec vitam sine Marte pati, quippe omnis in armis
Lucis causa sita, & damnatum viuere paci.
Venit & Aurora lachrymis perfusus in orbem
Diuersum, patrias fugit cum deuius oras
Armiger Eoi non felix Memnonis Astyr:
p.note: Astyr, vnde Astures. Astures opti-mi equites.
p.i: His paruus sonipes, nec Marti notus: at idem
Aut inconcusso glomerat vestigia dorso,
Aut molli pacata celer trahit effeda collo.

page.notes: Marginal notes are printed in the right margin; the notes given here are as printed. The "A 4" mark is a gathering signature. Some verse letters are faint and may be misread; the Greek-letter ornaments are rendered as printed.
